assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law-and-finance research supplied an influential framework for understanding how investor protection and legal institutions shape corporate finance and development.
assessment.attribution: La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny form the central collaboration; the proposed three capture a substantial but necessarily selective share of that joint contribution.
assessment.maturity: The work has been extensively used across finance, development and policy research over several decades.
uncertainties: The appropriate allocation of credit within the four-person core group is difficult.
Causal interpretation and the durability of legal-origin claims remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work transformed analysis of over-the-counter markets, search frictions and credit risk, with direct relevance to modern financial-market design.
assessment.attribution: Duffie, Pedersen and Garleanu made identifiable complementary theoretical contributions to the listed research program.
assessment.maturity: Its models have become durable reference points and gained added practical salience through financial-market disruptions.
uncertainties: The breadth of the research program makes a single prize formulation challenging.
Empirical separation of particular mechanisms is sometimes difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The analysis of collateral constraints and financial amplification gave macroeconomics a powerful explanation for how credit conditions propagate real fluctuations.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provide the foundational collateral mechanism, while Gertler is central to the financial-accelerator formulation; the proposed allocation is intellectually coherent.
assessment.maturity: The mechanisms have been deeply incorporated into macro-finance research and policy analysis, particularly since the global financial crisis.
uncertainties: Simon Gilchrist is also a key contributor to the listed financial-accelerator work.
The relative empirical importance of alternative amplification mechanisms varies across episodes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on household balance sheets and mortgage debt made household leverage central to understanding credit booms, consumption collapses and macroeconomic vulnerability.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clearest joint contributors to the empirical household-debt agenda, with Campbell a major contributor to mortgage-finance foundations.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has strongly influenced macro-finance research and policy discussion since the financial crisis.
uncertainties: The candidate formulation combines related but partly distinct research programs.
The quantitative importance of debt-driven demand channels remains model- and setting-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel and GMM methods provided broadly consequential tools for credible empirical work where persistence, endogeneity and unobserved heterogeneity coincide.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell and Bond have closely connected and readily recognizable contributions to the core methods.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, exceptionally widely used and have generated a large literature on diagnostics and refinement.
uncertainties: Widespread application has also revealed finite-sample and instrument-proliferation problems.
The case for a prize depends on judging methodological impact against other econometric advances.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The study of liquidity, funding constraints and asset prices has reshaped understanding of how intermediary balance sheets affect market prices and systemic stress.
assessment.attribution: Amihud established central liquidity measurement and pricing insights, while Brunnermeier and Pedersen developed influential mechanisms linking market and funding liquidity.
assessment.maturity: These ideas have had sustained influence in asset pricing, banking and financial-stability analysis.
uncertainties: The work spans a broad literature rather than one tightly bounded discovery.
Overlap with other macro-finance candidates complicates a distinct award citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The research made management practices and organisational capital measurable economic objects and demonstrated their importance for productivity and firm performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom and Van Reenen are foundational to the measurement and empirical program, and Sadun has made major related contributions.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been replicated across countries and used to inform research on firms, productivity and policy.
uncertainties: Survey-based measurement and causal interpretation of management practices remain contested.
Credit allocation within the wider management-practices literature is not straightforward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework offered a tractable and influential account of how distorted allocation across firms can generate large productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are central to the seminal empirical framework, with Restuccia an important contributor to its broader theoretical and quantitative development.
assessment.maturity: The framework has produced a substantial cross-country and within-country literature and remains a standard benchmark.
uncertainties: Measured wedges may combine genuine distortions with measurement error or model misspecification.
The magnitude of misallocation's aggregate effects remains sensitive to assumptions.
